findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5167 is 'Upgrade Universal Forwarder (Windows)'; Splunk Connect for Kubernetes is an archived GitHub Helm chart that reached End of Support on 1 January 2024, yet it is named as the primary collector.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 6264; k8s_events and k8sobjects receivers) the primary collector and drop SCK/5167 from app and dataSources.

findings.explanation: The deployment controller records ScalingReplicaSet events against the Deployment object itself (message 'Scaled up replica set <rs> to N'), so involvedObject.name is already the deployment name; stripping the last hyphen segment truncates names such as 'payments-api' to 'payments' and merges distinct deployments.
findings.quote: These events carry `involvedObject.name` (the ReplicaSet name, from which the **deployment name** is derived by stripping the trailing hash).
findings.suggested_fix: State that involvedObject.kind=Deployment and involvedObject.name is the deployment name; only parse the ReplicaSet from the message if needed.

findings.explanation: ScalingReplicaSet is also emitted when an HPA or `kubectl scale` changes replicas, not only on rollouts, so autoscaling activity is counted as deployment velocity; the SURGE explanation even lists 'automated scaling events' as a cause. A rollout signal should key on new ReplicaSet creation / observedGeneration change.
findings.quote: The primary SPL counts distinct deployments per day from **ScalingReplicaSet** events.
findings.suggested_fix: Count rollouts from audit events on deployments with a spec (image/template) change, or from k8sobjects observedGeneration increments, and note that pure scale events are excluded.

findings.explanation: NewReplicaSetAvailable and ProgressDeadlineExceeded are reasons on the Deployment's Progressing condition; it is not clear they are emitted as Event reasons, in which case kube:events will never contain them and the success/failure search loses its main rollout outcomes.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the deployment controller source / a live cluster; if they are condition reasons only, source them from kube:deployment:status (status.conditions[].reason) instead of kube:events.

findings.explanation: The success numerator sums per-pod SuccessfulCreate and every ScalingReplicaSet event, while failures include per-pod BackOff from any crash-looping workload; the ratio is dominated by pod churn, not deployment outcomes, so the 90% threshold in implementation does not measure change failure rate.
findings.quote: A namespace with a `success_rate` below 90% likely has **broken CI/CD pipelines**
findings.suggested_fix: Define success/failure per rollout (one outcome per deployment generation) before computing success_rate, and describe that in implementation.

findings.explanation: Deployment change events fit Change (All_Changes); nothing maps to the host Performance model.
Marked verified by an agent reviewer while the deployment-name derivation and eval field references would produce wrong results on real event data.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until validated by an SME on a live cluster.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `coalesce(..., involvedObject.namespace, ...)` and `coalesce(involvedObject.name, ...)` use unquoted dotted field names; in eval '.' is the concatenation operator, so these evaluate as involvedObject . name (null) and silently fall through. Dotted JSON fields must be single-quoted ('involvedObject.name').

`mvindex(split(deployment, "-"), 0, mvcount(...)-2)` strips the last segment of the deployment name (involvedObject is the Deployment for ScalingReplicaSet), merging distinct deployments and returning a multivalue rather than a re-joined string; dc() then counts name fragments.

Attribution search counts every create/update/patch on deployments, including controller-manager status-subresource updates and HPA scale-subresource patches; filter objectRef.subresource and exclude system:serviceaccount:kube-system:* users. `user.groups{}` is not a deployer identity and should not be a fallback.

summary: A useful DORA-style velocity idea, but the deployment-name derivation rests on a wrong claim about ScalingReplicaSet events, the success/failure ratio mixes per-pod and per-rollout signals (and autoscaling), eval references to dotted field names are unquoted, and the collector/Splunkbase facts are wrong.
